title: Onboarding spec for incrementally-versioned open models and pinning behavior
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Clarify product requirements and acceptance criteria for onboarding open models that publish incremental versions (x.y, x.y+1, x.y+patch). Define pinning semantics (hard/soft), automated compatibility metadata, and required artifacts so the Catalog and runtime can reliably serve model variants and fallbacks.
scope: This ticket defines required metadata, verification steps, and UX expectations for onboarding open models that will receive frequent incremental releases. It covers pin semantics, fallback mapping, compatibility note structure, required artifacts (sample inputs, quantization artifacts, sharding hints), and automated checks integrated into model intake. It also defines the acceptance criteria that enable Catalog entries to be marked production-ready for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
out_of_scope: Onboarding process changes for proprietary closed-source models, runtime kernel optimizations, and major catalog UI redesigns. Not covering billing/pricing changes related to new model variants.
requirements: Model entry must include explicit versioning field following semver-like pattern (major.minor.patch).
Provide two pinning options: 'hard_pin' (exact version only) and 'soft_pin' (allow minor/patch upgrades within compatible range).

Compatibility notes must include: supported sequence lengths, required tokenization artifacts (vocab/merges), quantization-tested precisions (e.g., int8, q4_0), and any architecture caveats (multi-GPU, sharded weights).
Each onboarding package must include a minimal smoke-test bundle: 5 canonical prompts, expected token-length distribution, and a small golden-output or deterministic hash for reproducibility.
Automated compatibility checklist that runs during intake: tokenization sanity, model load under target memory budget, one-step generation with stable RNG seed, and KV cache warmup simulation.
Fallback map: catalog must accept an explicit 'fallbacks' list linking compatible older/newer variants and a priority order for routing when preferred variant is unavailable.
Manifest must surface a 'compatibility_score' (low/medium/high) and a short free-text 'compatibility_notes' field for human context.

Onboarding UI should expose pin options to customers with an inline explanation of tradeoffs and recommended default ('soft_pin' to minor version only) and a checkbox to enable automatic minor patches.
acceptance_criteria: Given a sample open model artifact, the intake pipeline accepts a manifest that includes version, pinning setting, compatibility_score, and fallback list. Entry moves into 'candidate' state without manual gating.

Automated checks pass: tokenization roundtrip, model loads under declared memory budget, and smoke-test outputs match provided golden hashes within deterministic tolerance. Failure produces actionable error with recommended fixes.

If 'hard_pin' is selected, runtime routing returns 404-style variant-mismatch when a request specifies an unavailable version; if 'soft_pin' is selected, runtime routes to highest compatible minor/patch within declared range. Test cases cover both behaviors.
Catalog UI surfaces compatibility_score and an explainer tooltip; users can toggle pin mode during deployment and see the effective fallback order. UX validated by PM + 1 design review.

At least one model onboarding following this spec completes end-to-end into Hosted and Dedicated staging with monitored metrics: successful inference, matching tokenization, and no silent degradation in outputs over sample prompt set.

Acceptance tests include an automated job that verifies fallback behavior by simulating primary variant OOS (out-of-service) and asserting routing to next valid fallback occurs without user intervention.
success_metrics: Time-to-acceptance for open-model intake reduced to <= 2 business days (from submission to candidate state) for compliant packages.
Number of rollback incidents caused by unintended minor/patch upgrades reduced by 90% for models onboarded under this spec.
Increase in the percentage of catalog entries with complete compatibility metadata to 95% within one quarter of spec rollout.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Upfront burden on community contributors to supply artifacts may reduce submissions. Mitigation: provide a lightweight 'quick-accept' path that collects missing artifacts asynchronously while marking entry as 'provisional' with limited routing.
Risk: Incorrect compatibility_score or missing fallback maps could cause routing surprises. Mitigation: require automated checks and a manual triage checkbox for first 2 releases of a model.

Risk: Runtime complexity from supporting both hard and soft pin semantics. Mitigation: limit 'soft_pin' to minor/patch automatic upgrades by default and provide clear telemetry on when automatic upgrades occurred.
